candidates.role: Senior Researcher and Co-Director, National Resource Center for Alaska Native Elders; Assistant Professor, Center for Human Development, University of Alaska Anchorage
candidates.org: Southcentral Foundation (primary for this paper); UAA (secondary)
candidates.anchorage_tie: Based in Anchorage; Southcentral Foundation at 4085 Tudor Centre Drive, Anchorage, AK 99508; UAA office also in Anchorage bowl
candidates.decision_what_happened: Hiratsuka served as corresponding author on 'Artificial intelligence/machine learning in Alaska Native healthcare systems: symposium perspectives,' published May 23, 2026 in the International Journal of Circumpolar Health. The paper formally establishes a tribal-sovereignty-first AI governance framework for the Alaska Tribal Health System, endorsing community-engaged AI development over unilateral commercial AI adoption. Records three concrete commitments: sharing of ANTHC statewide AI use policy, documentation of Cerner AI Scribe implementation in primary care, and collaboration via Shared Tribal Analytics and Reporting (STAR) meetings. NIH award 1OT2OD032581-01.
candidates.binary_owned: Publish/formalize a tribal-sovereignty-first AI governance framework for the Alaska Tribal Health System — Hiratsuka as corresponding author and program PI endorsed and published this framework
candidates.ak_consequence: Healthcare sector — establishes governance architecture governing AI adoption across the Alaska Tribal Health System, serving approximately 175,000 Alaska Native people; sets precedent for AI vendors entering ATHS market to comply with tribal data sovereignty requirements
candidates.primary_source_outlet: PubMed Central / International Journal of Circumpolar Health

corroborating_sources.outlet: Frontiers in AI — companion paper, same team, April 2025

candidates.prelim_debatable_axis: Tribal-sovereignty-first AI governance protects Alaska Native data from commercial exploitation vs. potentially slowing AI adoption vs. peer health systems; STAR coordination mechanism is informal; 31-participant qualitative consensus may not produce technical specs for production-grade AI
candidates.scout_pre_screen_notes: Decision is journal paper publication documenting 2025 symposium — not a discrete binary institutional decision. Single-sourced to journal publication. No ANTHC press release, NIH award announcement in window, or SCF board vote. Weak decision framing.

candidates.org: Alaska Airlines (HQ Seattle, WA; major hub at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport)
candidates.anchorage_tie: Alaska Airlines operates one of its largest maintenance hubs at Ted Stevens Anchorage International; Engel's role covers all maintenance operations including Anchorage base. Subject himself appears Seattle/Portland-area-based per career history — bowl tie is operational impact of his decision, not personal residency.
candidates.decision_what_happened: Alaska Airlines announced investment and multiyear partnership with Tailsight AI-powered maintenance planning platform (April 16, 2026). Alaska is the first major airline to deploy the platform. Uses high-speed optimization engine to generate maintenance plans accounting for real-world constraints of labor, parts, station capability, and aircraft readiness.
candidates.binary_owned: Vendor-select and invest: chose to invest in Tailsight and deploy as first-mover airline customer, over competing/in-house approaches; Engel as VP Maintenance Ops owns the decision
candidates.ak_consequence: Aviation sector; Anchorage is Alaska Airlines' major northern hub; maintenance planning decisions affect AOG time and operational reliability at Anchorage and 100+ other stations; investment amount undisclosed

subject_quotes.verbatim: What gives me the most confidence is the team behind the product. For nearly two years, we have worked closely together to define requirements, shape the software and test it in real-world conditions.
subject_quotes.context: Engel quoted in the April 16, 2026 official Alaska Airlines press release

candidates.prelim_debatable_axis: First-mover advantage in AI maintenance planning vs. undisclosed investment amount and unclear timeline for Anchorage-specific AOG improvements; Alaska Airlines Anchorage hub reliability affects connections for all Interior and Bush Alaska traffic
candidates.scout_pre_screen_notes: Bowl requirement uncertain — Engel appears Seattle-based, not Anchorage-bowl. Decision date April 16 is 10 days outside 60-day window; in-scope for 90-day window. Prior cycle failures were on corroboration (Gate 4) — NOW RESOLVED with ePlaneAI and Investing.com as independent sources. Main gate issue is Anchorage bowl residency/work.

candidates.role: Dean, College of Engineering; Professor of Computer Science; Co-Director, Alaska Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Lab (ADSAIL); Principal Investigator, NSF RAISE Alaska AI Solutions Consortium (Award #2433241)
candidates.anchorage_tie: Full-time faculty and dean at UAA Anchorage campus; offices in EIB 403C and ECB 308C, 3211 Providence Drive, Anchorage, AK 99508
candidates.decision_what_happened: Mock co-organized and headlined the UAA/Dell AI Showcase on April 21, 2026, presenting the vision for 'AI-driven Engineering and Business Education at UAA.' As RAISE PI, Mock's program selected AY25/26 community-partner mini-grant awardees through competitive proposal. The showcase also featured a Dell Technologies partnership that provides AI computing resources (including NVIDIA GPUs) to UAA researchers and students. UAA announced it would use Dell AI infrastructure to expand RAISE program capacity and student AI research access.
candidates.binary_owned: Mock as Dean and RAISE PI owns: (a) the selection of AY25/26 RAISE community mini-grant awardees, (b) the Dell infrastructure partnership that expands UAA's AI compute resources, and (c) the program direction of UAA's AI education and community engagement strategy
candidates.ak_consequence: Education/AI research sector; RAISE community mini-grants channel AI research capacity to named Alaska community organizations; ADSAIL governs UAA's data science curriculum serving 500+ students; Dell partnership provides NVIDIA GPU access to Anchorage-based researchers for the first time at scale; timeframe: AY2025-2026 ongoing

corroborating_sources.outlet: Alaska Public Media — independent coverage of Mock's RAISE program (Sept 2025)

subject_quotes.verbatim: What we're doing is we're asking the community, 'What are what kind of problems do you have that potentially could be addressed with AI?'
subject_quotes.context: Mock describing the RAISE community-engagement approach to Alaska Public Media, September 2025

candidates.prelim_debatable_axis: Community-first AI framing (asking what problems to solve) vs. vendor-partnership approach (Dell/NVIDIA showcase may be as much marketing as program direction); NSF RAISE grants are small ($5K-25K mini-grants) vs. scale of Alaska's AI needs
candidates.scout_pre_screen_notes: April 21 showcase is 5 days outside 60-day window; in-scope for 90-day. Decision binary is soft — showcase event not a discrete approve/block/fund/hire. The RAISE AY25/26 community awardee selection is the right decision but announcement date unconfirmed. Dell partnership at showcase is closer to a discrete decision but is primarily a vendor announcement.

candidates.role: Vice President, NASA and NOAA Operations
candidates.org: ASRC Federal (subsidiary of Arctic Slope Regional Corporation, Anchorage-headquartered ANC)
candidates.anchorage_tie: ASRC (Arctic Slope Regional Corporation) maintains administrative HQ in Anchorage; Morad is an Alaska Native Iñupiaq ASRC shareholder raised in Anchorage. However, Morad himself currently works from Hartford, CT, not the Anchorage bowl. ASRC Federal is based in Huntsville, AL. Bowl tie is through ASRC corporate parent only.
candidates.decision_what_happened: ASRC Federal Data Network Technologies LLC was selected by NOAA to execute the Financial Management Data System (FMDS) Technical Support Services contract (April 22, 2026). FMDS uses AI/ML to analyze prior spending data, predict future spending needs, and leverage a commercially developed custom AI module to analyze financial data patterns for individual contracts.
candidates.decision_window: 60-day (April 22 is 4 days OUTSIDE 60-day window; in 90-day window)
candidates.binary_owned: Contract win: ASRC Federal was selected over competitors for the NOAA FMDS AI-enabled financial management contract
candidates.ak_consequence: Federal IT contracting; ASRC is an Anchorage-administered ANC; contract win adds to ANC contract portfolio; no explicit dollar figure in this announcement (related FMDS bridge contract was $27M per prior reporting)

subject_quotes.verbatim: This contract award underscores NOAA's trust in our team to deliver innovative, reliable solutions like AI analytics for financial management
subject_quotes.context: Morad quoted in the April 22, 2026 ASRC Federal press release

candidates.prelim_debatable_axis: ASRC as Alaska Native ANC winning AI-enabled federal contracts represents ANC capacity building in federal tech services; however, the decision-maker is Hartford-based and the benefit flows to ASRC Federal (Huntsville), not directly to Anchorage bowl economy
candidates.scout_pre_screen_notes: Primary source is subject-controlled press release. Morad is Hartford, CT based — bowl requirement not met. Decision April 22 is 4 days outside 60-day window; in 90-day window.

candidates.role: Co-Founder and Chief Medical Information Officer
candidates.anchorage_tie: MyEyesAI headquarters at 542 W 2nd Ave, Anchorage, AK 99501. Rosen is Alaska's only board-certified, fellowship-trained orbital/oculoplastic and neuro-ophthalmologist, practicing at Ophthalmic Associates (same address). Bowl-based.
candidates.decision_what_happened: MyEyesAI, co-founded by Rosen, was selected as one of 10 companies in the Harvard Alumni Entrepreneurs (HAE) Accelerator (powered by Pegasus Tech Ventures) 5th cohort from 132+ applications (equity-free program). The company presented at Demo Day on May 13, 2026 and has been executing Q2 2026 pilots at Anchorage-area clinics (2 letters of intent signed with unnamed Anchorage clinics for ophthalmology AI triage). Rosen's clinical pilot ran 68+ patient visits with 95%+ diagnostic accuracy. MyEyesAI completed gBETA Alaska accelerator in March 2026.
candidates.decision_window: 60-day (Demo Day May 13; LOI signings Q2 2026 — exact dates unconfirmed)
candidates.binary_owned: Rosen chose to commit MyEyesAI to live clinical AI triage pilots at Anchorage clinics (accepting clinical risk and regulatory exposure) and to sign LOIs with Anchorage-area ophthalmology practices for Q2 2026 deployment without FDA clearance as a diagnostic device
candidates.ak_consequence: Healthcare sector; two Anchorage-area ophthalmology clinics entering AI-assisted triage pilots; Alaska has only one board-certified neuro-ophthalmologist statewide (Rosen himself); if LOIs convert to full deployment, AI platform would be live in Alaska patient-care settings for the first time
candidates.prelim_debatable_axis: Deploying AI triage at Anchorage clinics where specialist access is acutely scarce (Alaska has no optometric capacity surplus) vs. MyEyesAI has no FDA 510(k) clearance; 68 patients is thin validation base for clinical deployment; the LOI clinics are unnamed and unverifiable from public sources
candidates.scout_pre_screen_notes: The specific Q2 2026 LOI signing is referenced only as forward-looking in a March 11 article (outside window) — no independently-documented completed LOI with a specific in-window date. HAE Demo Day May 13 is in-window and corroborated but represents a pitch event, not a discrete clinical decision. Main issue: the clinical deployment decision lacks a documentable date and independent confirmation.
